findings.title: A restored hub backup can activate empty history
findings.impact: Data loss reproduced on disposable copies
findings.scenario: Create a normal hub backup while ownership is legacy or copying, with no completed destination. Restore that snapshot, then run normal migration.
findings.observed: Backup sanitation removed the only source events while keeping the pending locator. Both hub and computer accept active ownership, epoch 2, with cleanup complete and zero original events.
findings.cause: Backup sanitation deletes all legacy content regardless of whether durable computer ownership exists. Restore has no proof that its now-empty source lost data.
findings.fix: Prevent publication of a supposedly recoverable snapshot that strands pending content. Preserve a valid transition recovery source or fail backup explicitly; reject empty cutover when required source proof is missing. Keep the post-cutover hub content-free.
findings.test: storage-stability-audit.test.ts — restoring a new hub backup… (legacy / copying)

findings.title: A disconnect after commit can wedge the entire computer
findings.impact: Chat reopen, another healthy task, and terminal stop all fail
findings.scenario: Hub commits active ownership, then connection drops before computer receives migration.activate. Restart computer and hub services.
findings.observed: Computer remains prepared. Recovery requests its metadata snapshot before resuming activation; snapshot rejects prepared owner. Every retry repeats the same ordering. Global barrier also blocks pty.kill.
findings.cause: recoverComputer drains metadata for active hub locators before reconciling their pending destination activation.
findings.fix: Reconcile committed activation before metadata recovery. Require matching identity/epoch/hash proof and activation ACK before source cleanup. Keep repair and stop paths usable without weakening deletion fences.
findings.test: computer-chat-stability-audit.test.ts — interrupted activation (three failing cases + passing ordering control)

findings.title: Restoring an older hub cannot resume its prepared destination
findings.impact: Permanent migration conflict despite intact source data
findings.scenario: Computer stages migration; restore an older hub locator from before beginMigration. Original source content remains intact. Restart and run ownership recovery.
findings.observed: Recovery ignores prepared inventory. Hub generates a fresh migration ID; destination refuses overwrite of its original prepared store. Fresh coordinator and restart do not resolve the conflict.
findings.cause: Prepared state is not reconciled against restored legacy ownership; migration identity is regenerated.
findings.fix: Recover matching uncommitted migration proof under authenticated task/computer ownership. Reuse the original stage, or safely discard only a proven uncommitted stale stage. Never overwrite an active owner.

findings.title: An attachment edit can permanently strand migration
findings.impact: Both normal reads and migration retries stay blocked
findings.scenario: A legacy attachment lacks a pinned hash. Destination stages history; transfer.finish reply is lost. Edit the source artifact, then retry and restart.
findings.observed: The same migration emits a different manifest because current_version_id changed. Prepared destination keeps original hash and rejects the replacement manifest. Source survives, but normal routing cannot open it.
findings.cause: Attachment versions are resolved from mutable artifact HEAD during repeated export passes and retries, outside the frozen metadata checkpoint.
findings.fix: Freeze the attachment version mapping before the first export. Use that same immutable mapping and manifest on every retry while allowing unrelated artifact editing to continue.
findings.test: migration-stability-audit.test.ts — migration resumes prepared legacy attachment…

findings.title: Migration can return the wrong attachment bytes
findings.impact: Draft current version becomes an older version
findings.scenario: One artifact has two valid versions: an older pinned message reference and a current draft reference without contentHash. Migrate both versions.
findings.observed: Both blobs arrive correctly, but draft retains its bare reference. Computer attachment reader selects the first matching artifact record and returns older bytes. Reproduced with both artifact version rows present.
findings.cause: Export creates separate sealed attachment records without sealing references embedded in drafts/events/queues/settings. Bare reads are ambiguous across versions.
findings.fix: Rewrite all embedded references using the frozen version mapping. Preserve explicitly pinned history and reject unresolved ambiguous references.
findings.test: storage-stability-audit.test.ts — legacy draft attachment keeps current bytes…

findings.title: Old chat content on terminal-mode tabs never migrates
findings.scenario: A tab contains old hub chat events/draft, but user previously continued it in Claude Code or Codex terminal. Run two idle migration sweeps and forced recovery.
findings.observed: All four synthetic cases retain source content without a computer owner. Real corpus contains 1,687 such events on 11 tabs. Prompt history can migrate successfully while these per-tab rows remain.
findings.cause: Migration census and tab selection filter current tab mode, rather than enumerating stored content by identity. These are hub chat rows, not provider-managed native transcripts.
findings.fix: Enumerate every legacy content-bearing tab across source tables. Preserve history identity independently of current display/agent mode; do not create unwanted visible chats.
findings.test: migration-stability-audit.test.ts — idle migration covers old chat rows… (four cases)

findings.title: A prepared tab can steal an active tab’s configuration
findings.impact: Wrong model read; configuration writes fail
findings.scenario: Active chat shares a task/provider with another prepared store whose storage ID sorts earlier.
findings.observed: Active tab reads prepared tab’s model instead of its own. Writes throw Conversation prepared.
findings.cause: taskTab excludes deleted/inbox stores but includes prepared stores and chooses by storage ordering.
findings.fix: Restrict normal task operations to active eligible stores. Prefer explicit tab/root context when several stores share a task.

findings.title: One incomplete transfer disables all computer backups
findings.impact: Unrelated healthy history cannot be backed up
findings.scenario: A prepared conversation references an attachment whose bytes have not arrived. Request a computer backup containing other active history.
findings.observed: Backup enumerates the prepared reference and fails ENOENT. Existing completed backups remain intact.
findings.cause: Backup creation includes incomplete staged records without a coherent completeness policy.
findings.fix: Snapshot complete recoverable stores consistently, or explicitly report deferred content without disabling backup of unrelated healthy history. Never publish a partial archive as complete.

findings.title: Reconnect creates unsolicited visible chat tabs
findings.impact: 574 generated tabs already present in current snapshot
findings.scenario: A native-only task gets background prompt-history storage, then computer ownership recovery runs.
findings.observed: Storage-only prompt-history:<task> is materialized as a visible Claude Chat tab. Pre-upgrade snapshot had zero; current snapshot has 574. A fresh upgrade replay creates 567 on reconnect.
findings.cause: Recovery treats all non-artifact, non-inbox owners as displayable terminal tabs.
findings.fix: Represent storage purpose explicitly and suppress UI tab creation for prompt-only stores. Repair generated bindings without deleting history or discarding later user activity.

findings.title: Migration failure looks like normal progress
findings.impact: User sees an indefinite moving spinner instead of the error
findings.scenario: Chat availability is migrating and a read fails with an actionable migration error.
findings.observed: ChatStorageNotice shows generic status detail and omits the actual load error.
findings.cause: Status detail takes precedence over error even after migration has failed.
findings.fix: Show the failure reason and retry state alongside location/status; distinguish failed work from active progress. Preserve diagnostics privacy.

findings.title: An incomplete backup can be published as a verified archive
findings.impact: Restored archive claims verification but lacks attachment bytes
findings.scenario: Remove a blob file and its manifest entry while leaving its SQLite attachment reference intact.
findings.observed: Restore accepts and publishes the archive. Wrong scope, duplicate entries, missing database, and corrupt listed blobs are correctly rejected.
findings.cause: Verification hashes listed files and checks SQLite integrity/FKs, but does not prove that all database blob references are represented in the manifest.
findings.fix: Cross-check every attachment/artifact-version reference against the verified file set before archive publication. Keep previous archives intact on failure.
findings.test: lifecycle-stability-audit.test.ts — archive publication rejects an omitted blob…

findings.title: An empty metadata poll takes over a second
findings.impact: Repeated synchronous work delays normal chat operations
findings.scenario: Call pendingMetadata on a private copy of the actual computer database with 72,920 settings records (~158 MiB retained JSON) and zero pending updates.
findings.observed: Three calls take 1,290 / 1,209 / 1,196 ms to return []. Largest owner snapshot reads ~33 MiB to return only 4.5 KiB of metadata. Synthetic 32 MiB control confirms scaling.
findings.cause: Handler loads/parses every settings value before filtering metadata:. Metadata snapshots similarly load all record kinds, including timelines/diagnostics. Post-write drains repeat this work.
findings.fix: Filter and project metadata/outbox records in SQL before decoding. Add appropriate indexes and bounded pagination; avoid retained content on control paths.

findings.title: Large-history export repeatedly sorts the whole conversation
findings.impact: Migration cost grows faster than history size
findings.scenario: Export history in 256-row batches through the actual legacy source query.
findings.observed: SQLite uses a temporary sort for each batch across three export passes. Isolated synthetic benchmark: 10k→40k events costs 33→427 ms; direct indexed seek costs 3→12 ms. Timing is illustrative; query-plan regression is deterministic.
findings.cause: seq+1 AS _rowid plus outer WHERE/ORDER BY prevents sequence range seek.
findings.fix: Page directly on (tab_id, seq) using the existing index. Preserve deterministic ordering and bounded transfer chunks.
